Witch Art Lab

Night in the forest: twilight everywhere, and the witch's glow shows the true colours near her. Pick the variant you like best and it becomes the new style; the next six grow from it. Drag knobs to steer by hand.

Pick one

Map

A whole run's forest: 20 × 20 areas cut by Boris the Brave's fractal jittered Voronoi. Each colour is an area type, never beside itself; white dots are area centres, where the clearings are; the ringed area in the middle holds the dancefloor. "New forest layout" draws a new map; "Border detail" sets how many fractal layers shape the borders.

Bestiary

Thirty forest animals, each as legend, adult, young and baby, in the current style under even light, turned towards you (or away, for creatures walking up the screen). Legends grow the magical features listed.

Sigils

Each creature's sigil: its name written in the forest's magic, in its own neon. Leashed creatures' sigils float above the witch, newest at the bottom; placing one writes it on the ground as the leashing rune, and picking it up lifts it back. The stack sways gently while she is still and trails behind her when she flies.

Below, each sigil at the four creature levels (baby, young, adult, legend), flat and then on the ground at the game's angle, drawing on.

Sprite sheet

Set pieces

Every area's set piece, its landmark, five to a row with the witch for scale. The twenty new ones are built in 3D at landmark size; the first ten are drawn smaller (the prototype scales those up).

Ground cover and wind

The area's ground-cover tufts, scattered thickly over its floor (each with its share of the area's tufts), drawn four times their size; then a few of its trees and leafy props. Beside each, its sway mask for the wind: black stays still (trunks, rocks), white sways most (the leafy tips).

Tall pieces

Something tall for the open areas that have no trees, standing sparsely among their mounds, boulders and logs: cairns and standing stones on the moor, pillars and a tall cairn at the stone shrine, dead snags hung with bracket fungi in the log pile, rock spires and a stalagmite in the ravine. Each row is an area's own big pieces, then the witch for scale; the last row is the Norway turf hut with its roof mended.

Relics

The modern world, reclaimed by the forest: cars, trolleys, cones, broken highway and odds and ends; the overgrown playground's pieces; the sports grounds' pieces (tennis, baseball, football, a basketball hoop). Then each arrangement as suggested, the witch at its middle.

Decorations

World decorations any area can have, placed sparsely as discoveries: twelve ruins (weathered, then overgrown), rocks, freak trees, and the lake kit (water, shore band, reeds, lily pads), with the witch for scale.

Farm, street and landmarks

Countryside and street decorations, single pieces: the farm (tractor, trailers, hay bales, fences, a gate, trough, water butt, scarecrow, churn, barrow, plough), the street (lampposts, one still flickering warm; signs blank or symbol-only; a bench, bin bags, a bus shelter), then the pieces the small scenes are built from, then the large scenes' pieces (cemetery, car park, scrap yard, the places of worship as far and near halves, castle, classical ruins), with the witch for scale.

Scenes

Scenes: a few related pieces arranged together, each counting as one piece on the map. Each is composed from reused piece sprites at its positions, the witch at its middle: the small ones, then the large ones at set-piece scale.

Genomes

Every species is now a genome record: its template (body plan), palette, proportions and parts as data. Below, ten species' adults each baked once as a material mask and coloured on the GPU at draw time from a palette row; pick a coat to recolour them all without rebaking. Click a creature to see its record.


      


      

        
Sleeping legends

        
Every area's legend asleep, centuries deep: sunk half into its area's earth, head down and eyes shut, its glow gone to stone and old wood, mossed, lichened and grown over, so it passes for a boulder, a log or a mound. Each row: asleep (two frames of a slow breath), the legend awake as it is, then the witch for scale.

        

      


      

        
Party objects

        
The party objects scattered over partified areas, at night as in the game: litter, the light sources (neon pieces in a different neon each), furniture and set dressing, with the witch for scale. Then a sample patch of party ground: clusters and loose objects strewn as the prototype might. Last, balloons unlit and then beside a lantern: they don't glow, they catch the light.

        

      


      

        
Paths

        
A path kind laid along a curve with a branch meeting it, as the game would sweep it; then its strip, end, Y and T junction textures; then the 3D pieces (edge props, stairs, bridges, railway landmarks), with the witch for scale.

        

        

      


      

        
Trees

        
An area's trees across their whole range of heights, from saplings to the occasional giant that pokes above the canopy, with the witch for scale, and how the area lays out its vegetation (its layout, which the prototype's generator reads).

        

        

      


      

        
Witch

        
The witch in every pose, turned towards you (top) and away (bottom): three frames of her hover, the fast-flight lean and its four-frame cycle (legs kicking, jacket and hair fluttering, bristles flickering), flying flat out over the treetops (three frames), braking hard (two frames), then rising to the treetops and descending to the ground, two frames each. Then flying straight up the screen (seen from behind) and straight down it (at you): three hover frames, the lean and its cycle, flat out (three) and braking (two). Below, on foot (towards, then away), after her hover for scale: standing (three idle frames), landing and taking off (three each), talking (four gestures), placing and lifting a sigil (three each), and sitting on her terrace (two).

        

      


      

        
Party witches

        
Witches who fly in to the party, one for each soundsystem: a row per party outfit (raver, flower child, disco, punk, festival, cat hat, glam, goth, candy, boho), each with its own hat, hair and top, its colours and skin picked by its seed (Shuffle picks others). With "a mix": hovering, the lean cycle, then a pose of each kind (dancing, drinking, running, hugging, sitting, stargazing). Pick a pose to see every frame of it, our witch first, then every outfit. Below, the pairs, put together at their anchors: dancing face to face, a hug, a high-five, holding hands (facing you), a toast, the conga, a twirl, and the broom limbo (two holding the broom, a third leaning back under it).

        

      


      

        
Party relics

        
Giant bottles, legend-sized and half-buried in the forest floor, 3 or 4 to a map, for the witch to find and dig up (#87). Each is its own shape and glass: a tall wine bottle (amethyst), a round flask (ruby), a square decanter (emerald), a tapering hexagonal bottle (sapphire), a spiral-fluted bottle (amber) and a teardrop potion (rose). The glass is see-through (its rim, a highlight, and a half-clear dither the ground shows through), and the liquid inside glows in its own colour, motes rising from the neck; in the game each lights the ground round it. Each is lit at night with its glint (a four-point star that comes and goes, so it can be spotted from the treetops) at its glint point; then the glint's frames, at the ground and treetop zooms; then their one sigil (the flask's silhouette: they all do the same in the game), bare and in each level's frame.

        

      


      

        
Flora

        
Trees grown from their plant genomes (art/flora/genomes.js). The new species come from the genome generator (art/flora/blob.js): levels of branches under a crown of 3 to 9 lit blobs filled with leaf stamps. They are wild cherry, crab apple, elder, aspen, whitebeam, field elm and cedar, and three fantasy trees: the glowcap (a mushroom tree with glowing gills), the crystal-leaf tree and the vinewood (hung with vines and glowing buds). Each row shows a sapling, young, mature and tall tree, lit at dusk; then its crown as the treetops show it, and its trunk as the ground shows it. Below is the chosen species' genome, to copy. In the game, ?flora=new (or fantasy, all, or a list of ids) grows them in every wooded area.

        

        

      


      

        
Witch generator

        
Witches grown from genome data (art/witchGenome.js): the hat (shape, crown height, brim, lean), hair, top, cloak (none, short, long, hooded), broom (classic, fan, twig or round bristles; the handle's length and bend; the bristles' length), accessories (headphones, sunglasses, glow sticks, a scarf, a satchel, a glowing pendant, earrings) and a palette from one base hue. The first is ours, drawn from her own genome exactly as she always is; the rest are generated (Reroll for others). Each hovers, leans and stands. Click one to see its genome, to copy.

        

        

      


      

        
Attack effects

        
What a fight looks like (Stage 5): projectiles (spit, a barb, a seed and a stone lobbed with their shadow, a feather dart, a glowing mote), short and long beams (start, the loop that repeats along the beam, end), the quake's ring and a spore cloud, the telegraphs (a target circle where a lob will land, a line along a beam or a charge with its start and arrowhead, the wind-up flash, the quake's reach), hit sparks, and the slow and knockback marks. Each row: its frames light (for the dark forest) on night ground, then dark (for bright ground) on a lit floor, then how the treetop camera shows it, the ground drawing and then the treetop one; ground decals also laid flat as the camera sees them. Tinted by the attack's side.

        

      


      

        
Home

        
The witch's treehouse, a tall timber tower of storeys up a giant tree, its witch's-hat tower standing above the treetops, with her sitting behind the decks in its cutaway DJ booth as the game starts: turned towards you, its base alone (as seen from the ground, under the canopy), and turned away. Below, the studio up close, where the game's camera starts.

        

      


      

        
Soundsystems

        
What the party defends: a sound-system stack hewn from magic stone, with glowing crystal cones. Each of the three stacks is shown playing (three frames of the cones pumping), damaged (two frames of flicker) and destroyed, with the witch for scale. Below them, the dancefloor speakers: one column each, twelve round the dancefloor, the far half facing in and the near half out so each shows us its front, drawn at three angles (15°, 45° and 75° from facing us; mirrored for the other side), playing, damaged and destroyed.

        

      


      

        
Dancefloor

          
          2
          
        

        
The hero floor: 30 tiles across, each lit by the tile-lighting engine. Here it plays the pattern library to a 120 bpm beat: on "the set", patterns that suit the party level, each in through a transition (wipe, iris, dissolve, or a burst on a bar line); or one picked pattern on a loop. Click the floor to stand the witch there (her own glow is a layer on top); click her again to clear. "Switch on" plays the boot-up sequence.
